_comment_top: HIL single-real-robot shared-exit experiment scope. Values copied here from source (cooperative_avoider.py / state_publisher.py declare_parameter defaults, confirmed by full source read 2026-07-23) are frozen and MUST match the shared, unmodified controller exactly -- this file records them for HIL launcher/guard config, it does not redefine them. Any field whose value is not yet backed by a real measurement on the physical unit or in the physical lab space is the literal string 'UNCONFIRMED_PHYSICAL_MEASUREMENT'. The motion launcher (run_hil_shared_exit_trial.sh) MUST refuse to run any ground-motion mode while any such field remains unconfirmed.

physical_unit.hardware: e-puck2 + Pi-puck + University of York expansion board + Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W

frozen_protocol._comment: Copied for reference only. Never edited here or anywhere for HIL -- source of truth is epuck2_comm_interfaces/msg/EpuckState.msg etc.
frozen_protocol.required_validity_flags_for_motion_note: ODOM alone is insufficient for ground motion: cooperative_avoider.py's local IR/ToF avoidance path is required (require_local_sensors=True in every N2/N3 controller launch, confirmed by source read), and the physical baseline batch's own recorded evidence (5/5 FINAL_PASS trials) shows validity_flags=7 was the actual steady-state value achieved on real hardware. hil_cmd_vel_guard.py's default --required-validity-flags is 7, not 1.

frozen_cooperative_avoider_params._comment: Copied from cooperative_avoider.py declare_parameter defaults, confirmed by full source read 2026-07-23. Never modified for HIL.

hil_guard_limits._comment: Independently enforced by hil_cmd_vel_guard.py; does not trust cooperative_avoider's own clamp.
hil_guard_limits.max_angular_speed_rps_note: Reset to UNCONFIRMED_PHYSICAL_MEASUREMENT 2026-07-23 after the suspended-wheel straight-line diagnostic test (SUSPENDED_WHEEL_DIAGNOSTIC_TEST_PASS, see suspended_wheel_diagnostic_20260723/SUMMARY.md) completed successfully -- that test used a temporary, explicitly test-scoped value of 0.0 rad/s (never a real measurement) which is not carried forward here per the user's own instruction that any turning/ground-motion test requires a separately measured and justified angular cap. No verified in-lab measurement of a safe turning rate exists yet; one known real data point is the Pi TCP bridge's own hard-coded watchdog ceiling logged during this session (limits 0.040m/s 2.000rad/s) -- that is a server-side safety limit, not a recommended guard value, and has not been adopted here.

coordinate_system._comment: Shared map frame that all EpuckState messages (real and virtual) are expressed in, per state_publisher.py's existing local_to_global() origin_x_m/origin_y_m/origin_yaw_rad parameters -- no new transform code needed, only correctly-measured origin parameters.
coordinate_system.units: metres, radians, ENU-style (x right, y forward on the physical table as viewed from the operator position -- to be fixed exactly during field measurement)
coordinate_system.virtual_peer_origin_note: Virtual peer runs in its own Webots/simulated frame that is DEFINED to coincide with the shared map frame (it has no separate physical offset to measure); only the real robot's origin requires a physical measurement.

clock_domains._comment: goal_navigator.py hardcodes rclpy.init with use_sim_time:=true, which never advances without a live /clock -- incompatible with real hardware. hil_topic_adapter.py instantiates GoalNavigator with a real-time (wall clock, use_sim_time:=false) rclpy context instead, without editing goal_navigator.py.
clock_domains.cross_domain_note: Because the two robots run on different clock sources, all cross-robot freshness checks in hil_cmd_vel_guard.py and hil_preflight.py compare each message's RECEIVE-side wall-clock timestamp (set by the receiving node's own clock), never the sender's embedded stamp -- this avoids any need for the two clocks to be synchronized or even comparable.

hil_comm_scope._comment: See HIL_DESIGN.md for the full frozen definition; duplicated here in compact form for launcher/guard config consumption.
hil_comm_scope.HIL_COMM_OFF: Physical robot never subscribes to the virtual peer's GoalAnnouncement topic; require_virtual_peer=false in the guard config; physical robot navigates using only its own state_publisher/goal_navigator/cooperative_avoider stack and local IR/ToF avoidance if the virtual peer enters its CPA-relevant EpuckState stream.
hil_comm_scope.HIL_COMM_ON: Physical robot's goal_navigator subscribes to the virtual peer's GoalAnnouncement topic (--goal-announcement-topic) in addition to everything HIL_COMM_OFF does; require_virtual_peer=true in the guard config.

field_geometry._comment: All UNCONFIRMED until Step 12 (post-wheel-suspension-test field measurement) is completed by the user. Do not fill in from the Webots N2/N3 world files -- those describe a simulated arena, not the physical lab space.
